images.section_title: Marking Pole Multiplicity on a Pole-Zero Plot
images.image_description: Create a clean 2D s-plane with Re(s) horizontal and Im(s) vertical axes, no grid clutter. Plot two real-axis poles at s=-1 and s=-4. Show one repeated pole marker at s=-1 indicating multiplicity 2 (for example a doubled symbol or label m=2). Show one simple pole marker at s=-4 with multiplicity 1 label m=1, and no other poles or zeros.

outline_section.section_title: Marking Pole Multiplicity on a Pole-Zero Plot
outline_section.learning_goal: Represent repeated poles on an $s$-plane diagram with an explicit multiplicity convention.

image_policy.image_description_seed: 2D pole-zero plot grid with real and imaginary axes and one repeated real pole location with duplicate or stacked marker notation.
visual_elements: unmarked pole point at repeat location
repeat-count marker (label $m=2 or two concentric symbols)$
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Generate a simple $s$-plane with one repeated and one simple pole so the writer can specify repeat marking conventions.

question_policy.practice_question_model: For $H(s)=\frac{4}{(s+2)^2(s-1)}$, mark each pole on an $s$-plane and choose the correct multiplicity notation for $s=-2$.
distractor_plan: Include one distractor that uses one marker for multiplicity greater than one.
Include one distractor that places the repeated pole in the wrong half-plane.
Include one distractor that uses a complex-conjugate pair marker pattern instead of real-axis repeat marking.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: For $H(s)=\frac{3}{(s+1)^2(s+4)}$, show the pole-zero plot and annotate each pole with multiplicity.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce a plot showing one repeated pole at $s=-1$ with multiplicity $2$ and one simple pole at $s=-4$ with multiplicity $1$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This extends algebraic multiplicity recognition into the plot layer with explicit diagram notation.
solution_step_plan: Factor and identify denominator roots and multiplicities.
Place each pole on the real axis in the $s$-plane.
Annotate repeated root at $s=-1$ with a consistent multiplicity marker.
practice_variation_axes: Move repeated and simple poles to different real locations.
Change multiplicity from 2 to 3 to require a reusable annotation rule.
Mix one left-half and one right-half-pole example for sign control.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Question generator should preserve a uniform repeat-notation convention across all lessons in this module.

images.lesson_core_move: Identify repeated roots of a transfer-function denominator as repeated poles and represent their multiplicity correctly on a pole-zero plot.
images.image_description: Create a 2D s-plane with Re(s) on the horizontal axis and Im(s) on the vertical axis, with subtle axis ticks. Plot the repeated complex-conjugate poles at s=-1+2j and s=-1-2j, marking each with the same multiplicity m=2 label. Use identical visual treatment for both conjugates (for example, paired doubled symbols or explicit annotation m=2) and keep other poles/zeros absent.

image_slot.image_description: Create a 2D s-plane with Re(s) on the horizontal axis and Im(s) on the vertical axis, with subtle axis ticks. Plot the repeated complex-conjugate poles at s=-1+2j and s=-1-2j, marking each with the same multiplicity m=2 label. Use identical visual treatment for both conjugates (for example, paired doubled symbols or explicit annotation m=2) and keep other poles/zeros absent.

outline_section.learning_goal: Count multiplicity for repeated complex-conjugate pole pairs and encode them correctly in the $s$-plane representation.

image_policy.image_description_seed: s-plane diagram with symmetric complex-conjugate poles, one pair shown with multiplicity greater than one.
visual_elements: symmetric conjugate poles above and below imaginary axis
multiplicity labels for each conjugate member
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use a small set of axis ticks and clear conjugate symmetry so multiplicity labeling is unambiguous.

question_policy.practice_question_model: If $H(s)=\frac{1}{\left(s^2+2s+5\right)^2}$, identify the repeated complex-conjugate poles and their multiplicities.
distractor_plan: Include one distractor that identifies only one root from the pair.
Include one distractor that labels multiplicity per conjugate pair incorrectly as 1.
Include one distractor that confuses repeated multiplicity with order of a denominator quadratic.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Find and plot the repeated complex-conjugate poles for $H(s)=\frac{1}{(s+1-2j)^2(s+1+2j)^2}$ with multiplicity annotations.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Recognize both $s=-1\pm 2j$ as repeated poles of multiplicity 2 each.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This extends multiplicity handling from the real axis to symmetric complex-conjugate locations in the complex plane.
solution_step_plan: Factor/parse quadratic factors into linear conjugate factors and identify each location.
Count multiplicity from exponent on each conjugate linear factor.
Plot both conjugates with matched multiplicity annotation.
practice_variation_axes: Vary complex shift and damping terms in conjugate factors.
Vary exponent 2, 3, and 4 on conjugate factors.
Contrast correct conjugate multiplicity against a single-factor complex pair distractor.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep conjugate pair symmetry explicit so the question generator can create mirrored variants without changing core mapping.
